overview: Black develops the c8-bishop to g4 before ...e6, pre-empting the Torre and London. White usually hits it with 3.Ne5, and after 3...Bf5 or ...Bh5 gains time or space with g4 or Qd3; Black must untangle without falling behind in development. It is a rare sideline and White tends to keep a small edge.

white_ideas.idea: 3.Ne5 to challenge the bishop and gain tempi, then g4 or Qd3 against Bf5/Bh5
Build the centre with c4 or e3 and Nc3 once the bishop has been displaced

black_ideas.idea: Get the bishop outside the pawn chain before ...e6, avoiding the London bishop trade problem
Challenge e5 with ...Nd7 and ...f6 or play for ...Bxf3 and a solid pawn structure

typical_structures.structure: White d4/e3 centre against Black d5/e6 with the bishop outside, or Queen's Gambit-type structure after c4

character.notes: Not forcing beyond 3.Ne5 and g4 skirmishes; positions are steady with White a little ahead in space and tempi. Not clearly solid or sharp.

soundness.notes: Playable but concedes tempi after Ne5; White is slightly better with correct play. Not refuted.

structure.notes: Centre stays in tension d4 against d5 and White can still play c4 or e3, so undecided.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom meet 1.d4 with an early Bg4; chosen mainly to leave main lines.

level.notes: Few moves to learn, but Black must know how to regroup the bishop and handle White's space.

sublines_that_differ.name: Anti-Torre main line
sublines_that_differ.how: White grabs space and kicks the bishop again; sharper than the quiet 3.e3 lines.

character.reason: Neither a forcing nor a rock-solid line; White keeps a mild initiative.

soundness.reason: Black is a little worse but not refuted.

structure.reason: The d4 and d5 pawns stay in tension and neither centre is decided.

approach.reason: Strong players rarely choose an early Bg4 here.

level.reason: Needs care regrouping the bishop but little theory.

plans.reason: White's tempo gains on the bishop shape the early play.
